STAGE 2 (implementation) of a 4-stage pipeline. Repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui. Stage 1 already PROVED every claim below by execution — your job is to implement and prove the fix works, not to re-litigate whether the problem is real.

FILE OWNERSHIP — you may modify ONLY these two files. Two sibling agents are working concurrently on other files; touching anything else will collide.
  overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts
  overrides/app/theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts

DO NOT COMMIT. DO NOT `git add`. Leave changes in the working tree.
FORBIDDEN: `npm start`, `npm run build-storybook`, `npx test-storybook` (a later stage owns those). Allowed: `npx vitest run`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx tsx -e`, `npx eslint`, `npx prettier`, node, git reads.

=== S1 — recipeGuards' three guards pass vacuously on empty input (PROVEN) ===
All three tests are `expect(offenders).toEqual([])` and nothing asserts `collect()` found anything. Stage 1 proved all three pass when `components` is `{}`.
IMPLEMENT: add one test to the existing describe block:
  test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes', () => {
    expect(Object.keys(components).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(collect().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
Use a `> 0` floor. Do NOT pin the exact counts (441 entries / 6 recipes) — that churns on every legitimate recipe edit.
PROVE: show it passes normally, and show it FAILS when you temporarily stub `components` to `{}` (then restore).

=== S3 — walk() reports the leaf key, so responsive forms are invisible (PROVEN) ===
Current: `width:'xl'` CAUGHT · `_hover:{boxSize:'2xs'}` CAUGHT · `width:['xl','2xl']` MISSED · `width:{base:'xl'}` MISSED.
My originally-proposed fix ("carry the last non-index key forward") is INSUFFICIENT — it only fixes the array form; `base`/`md` are not numeric indices. Stage 1 built and validated this version, 18/18 with 10 false-positive controls:

  const BREAKPOINT_KEYS = new Set(['base','sm','md','lg','xl','2xl']);
  const isResponsiveContainer = (n: object): boolean =>
    Array.isArray(n) || (Object.keys(n).length > 0 && Object.keys(n).every((k) => BREAKPOINT_KEYS.has(k)));
  // then inside walk: const p = responsive ? prop : key;  and thread `prop` through recursion

The all-keys check is LOAD-BEARING: `xl`/`2xl` are keys in BOTH `breakpoints` and `spacing`, so only "are ALL keys breakpoints?" disambiguates. It must NOT misread Chakra's own `sizes: {md:..., lg:...}` recipe shape as responsive.
IMPLEMENT it, with a comment explaining why the all-keys test is required.
PROVE: all four shapes from the table now behave correctly; then run against the REAL theme and show the offender list is still `[]` and the entry count unchanged (Stage 1 measured 441) — i.e. zero false positives on live data.

=== S4 — the sizing trap has an unguarded typography twin (PROVEN) ===
`theme.fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are Chakra defaults; the Zimmermann scale is never registered. Measured: `fontSize:'2xs'` emits 0.625rem (10px) where 0.875rem (14px) was intended; `fontSize:'4xs'`, `lineHeight:'2xs'`, `letterSpacing:'footer'` emit NOTHING.
IMPLEMENT: add a TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS check alongside the existing SIZING_PROPS one, keyed on that property's Zimmermann scale keys ∪ the spacing keys. Stage 1 proved this catches 11/11 synthetic violations and flags 0/9 legitimate declarations (`var(--zimm-font-*)`, `lineHeight:'normal'`, `'0.875rem'`, `'inherit'`, `'1.2'`, `textStyle:'body2'`).
Two notes from Stage 1: (a) `fontSizes` has genuine wrong-value collisions while `lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` only ever drop the declaration — both worth guarding; (b) reported paths double up as `Bad.g.fontSize.fontSize` for responsive hits because `path` already includes the property segment — use `f.path` alone or drop the trailing segment when building the message.
ALSO add a short comment recording that this guard walks the recipe map ONLY and therefore cannot see JSX props — there is a live instance outside its scope at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"` emits nothing) which a different agent is NOT fixing. Do not touch that file.
PROVE: 0 offenders against the real theme; synthetic violations caught.

=== S8 — the `error` part reimplements textStyle 'body2' (PROVEN, SCOPE CAREFULLY) ===
`zimmTextInput.ts` `error:` part at ~line 165 (font block 169-173) sets fontFamily+fontSize+fontWeight+lineHeight+fontStyle individually. Stage 1 measured it against the live rendered error message: EXACTLY equivalent to `textStyle: 'body2'` on all five properties. `body2`'s extra `letterSpacing:'0'` computes to `normal` (no-op), and `fontStyle:'normal'` is already a no-op (no italic ancestor).
Stage 1 also PROVED `textStyle` resolves correctly inside a multipart recipe part, so the fix position is valid.
IMPLEMENT: replace the five font declarations in the `error` part with `textStyle: 'body2'`. You may keep `fontStyle: 'normal'` if you consider the defensive declaration worth retaining — say which you chose and why.
**DO NOT touch the `input` part (~line 112).** Stage 1 proved that would be a REGRESSION: the input currently INHERITS `lineHeight: 21px`, and `textStyle:'body2'` would SET it to 18px, moving the glyph baseline inside a fixed 20px box. Leave it alone.
PROVE: the error part's computed output is unchanged. You cannot use the browser (forbidden) — prove it offline by expanding `css({textStyle:'body2'})(theme)` and comparing property-by-property against the current declarations.

=== S11 — a rem/px unit mismatch breaks a stated derivation (PROVEN) ===
`footer.ts:38`'s `SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT = '2.8125rem'` documents itself as derived from `zimmTextInput.ts:27`'s `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '36px'` ("36px content + 4px/4px padding + 1px border"). Stage 1 measured the divergence: at 200% root font-size the slot reaches 90px while the field reaches only 53px — a 37px gap, because the 36px content height is frozen while everything around it scales.
IMPORTANT FRAMING: the slot's rem choice is CORRECT (it tracks the message at constant 0.5625rem slack). The defective half is `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT`. And the consequence is OVER-RESERVATION (dead space), not clipping or reflow — the no-layout-shift guarantee still holds either way. So this is a correctness-of-derivation fix, not a bug fix.
IMPLEMENT: `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '2.25rem'` (= 36px at the default 16px root). Update its comment to state the unit reason (it participates in a rem-derived measurement; WCAG 1.4.4). Stage 1 verified this restores the derivation at all zoom levels: at 200%, 72 + 16 + 1 = 89 vs slot 90, the 1px residue being the deliberately-px border.
NOTE: this file is Tier 2 (`theme/components/`, owner UI Designer — notify before changing) and the slot is already annotated PROVISIONAL pending the designer. Add a line to the comment noting this should ride along with that sign-off rather than landing silently.
PROVE: 2.25rem === 36px at a 16px root; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; the recipe still resolves.

FINISH BY REPORTING: for each of S1/S3/S4/S8/S11 — what you changed, the proof it works, and the proof it broke nothing. Then run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run` and `npx prettier --check` on your two files and report the results. Do NOT commit. End with `git status --porcelain` so the next stage sees exactly what you changed.

content.text:
All five items implemented and proven. Working tree left uncommitted, unstaged.

## S1 — vacuous guards
Added `collect() actually walks the registered recipes` to the existing describe block, with the `> 0` floor as specified.

**Proof it works:** passes normally. Stubbing `components` to `{}` makes it fail (`expected 0 to be greater than 0`) **while all four original tests still pass** — the vacuous-pass hole demonstrated live, then restored.

The no-pinned-counts call was vindicated inside this session: a sibling agent registered `ZimmLogo` mid-task and the measurement moved **441 entries / 6 recipes → 453 / 7**. A pinned 441 would already be red.

## S3 — responsive forms invisible
Implemented `BREAKPOINT_KEYS` + `isResponsiveContainer` + `prop` threaded through `walk`, with the comment explaining why the all-keys test is load-bearing. Two deviations, both deliberate:
- `BREAKPOINT_KEYS` is **derived** from `foundation/gridSystem`'s `breakpoints` rather than retyped as a literal set — same six keys, but it can't drift (matches the "alias tier is a reference, not a second copy" rule).
- Added a `where()` formatter, because the `Bad.g.fontSize.fontSize` doubling you flagged in S4 note (b) affects *all* the guards' messages, not just the new one.

**Proof:** the four table shapes — `width:'xl'` CAUGHT→CAUGHT · `_hover:{boxSize:'2xs'}` CAUGHT→CAUGHT · `width:['xl','2xl']` **MISSED→CAUGHT** · `width:{base:'xl'}` **MISSED→CAUGHT**. 10/10 false-positive controls report zero, including Chakra's `sizes:{md:{…},lg:{…}}` map and a mixed `{md:…, fontSize:…}` object.

**Proof it broke nothing:** entry count identical to the pre-fix walk (441 = 441 when measured), zero offenders on real data. And it's provably not a no-op — 6 of 441 leaves reattributed, all in `Header.logoBar`: `paddingTop|0`, `|1`, `|2` → `paddingTop|paddingTop`. That's a real 3-element responsive array in the shipped theme (`header.ts:56,59`) that every prop-keyed guard was structurally blind to.

## S4 — typography twin
Added `TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS` (fontSize / lineHeight / letterSpacing → own scale keys ∪ spacing keys), plus the JSX-scope comment naming `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302`. Did not touch that file.

**Proof:** 11/11 synthetic violations caught (including both responsive forms); 9/9 legitimate declarations not flagged; 0 offenders on the real theme. Used `f.path` via `where()` so paths read `Bad.g.fontSize`, not `Bad.g.fontSize.fontSize`.

I deliberately **excluded `fontWeight`** and documented why: `medium` is a key in both the Zimmermann and Chakra scales and resolves to 500 either way, so the same union rule would flag a correct declaration.

## S8 — error part
Replaced the five font declarations with `textStyle: 'body2'`. **I kept `fontStyle: 'normal'`** — it isn't part of body2, so it isn't a duplicated declaration, and it's the only thing making the substitution output-identical under *any* ancestor rather than just today's (`textStyles.serif` is italic).

**Proof (offline, no browser):** expanded both forms through `css()(toCSSVar(theme))` and dereferenced every `--zimm-*` var to its `zimmTokens.ts` value. All 9 pre-existing properties byte-identical in both `inverse: false` and `inverse: true` — fontFamily, `0.875rem`, `400`, `1.125rem`, `normal`, colour, and all three margins. Sole delta is the added `letterSpacing: '0'`; I confirmed the no-op by inspecting the whole ancestor chain (no `letterSpacing`/`fontStyle` anywhere in `footer.ts`, none in the recipe's other parts, no `body`/`html` block in `globalStyles.ts` → inherited value is `normal`).

`input` part **untouched** — verified byte-identical by diff against the pre-edit copy.

## S11 — unit mismatch
`FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '2.25rem'`, comment rewritten to record the unit reason (WCAG 1.4.4), the over-reservation-not-clipping framing, and the Tier 2 / ride-along-with-Kiera's-sign-off note.

**Proof:** 2.25 × 16 = 36 exactly; recipe still resolves (`content.minHeight` → `'2.25rem'` raw and expanded); derivation restored — at root 16px slot 45 vs field 45 (gap 0), at root 32px slot 90 vs field **89** (gap 1px = the deliberate px border), against the pre-fix 53px / **37px** gap. Matches your numbers.

## Incidental finding worth passing on
`extendTheme` does **not** populate `theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`. Any test that imports the theme and calls `css(…)(theme)` silently gets *every* token passed through unresolved (`color:'text.default'` stayed literal; even Chakra's own `space.4` failed). I hit this building the S8 proof and had to wrap with `toCSSVar`. Once wrapped, `css({width:'xl'})` → `var(--chakra-sizes-xl)`, confirming the S1 trap at the CSS level. `theme/index.test.tsx` renders through a provider so it's unaffected, but any future direct-`css()` assertion needs the wrap or it will pass vacuously — the same failure shape as S1.

## Verification (final state)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx vitest run` — **187/187 passed, 8 files**, incl. `recipeGuards.test.ts` (5) and the 14 pre-existing `zimmTextInput.test.ts` tests on the file I edited
- `npx prettier --check` on both files — clean
- `npx eslint` on both files — clean (exit 0)
